title: Data: load, validate and snapshot the portfolio

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An export has two defects: one project's crew-months cell reads 'two', and two other projects each name the other as parent. What does the first snapshot attempt report?

options.text: Both defects, since the reader and the gate each report all they find in one pass
options.says: The gate runs only on a portfolio whose cells are clean; with six defects planted, the first attempt reported only the four cell errors.

options.text: Only the parent cycle, since a cycle blocks the export before its cells are converted
options.says: The cells are read first; the cycle is a gate rule, and the gate runs after the reader.

options.text: Only the crew-months cell, since the gate runs only once no cell has an error
options.says: Right: `snapshot` raises with the reader's findings before `gate` runs, so the cycle is found on the next attempt.

options.text: Neither, since the reader stops at the first row it cannot convert
options.says: That is what `gridcap.load_csv` does; the milestone's reader records a finding and keeps reading.

origin.section: Rules Across Projects Run Only on Clean Cells

questions.stem: A must-do project may start in 2030 or 2031 and spends $600k in its one year of work. The 2030 budget is typed as $500k; 2031's is correct, and nothing else is wrong. What does the gate's must-do spending rule report for 2030?

options.text: No finding, since the project can start in 2031 and spend nothing in 2030
options.says: Right: the rule adds each must-do's least spend over its start years, here 0 for 2030, so it never refuses a portfolio that has a plan.

options.text: An error, since the project's $600k is more than the 2030 budget
options.says: The rule takes the minimum over start years; refusing here would refuse a portfolio that has a plan, and the lesson calls the rule sound because it never does.

options.text: A warning, since the project could start in 2030 and overspend that year
options.says: The rule has one severity, error, and fires only when the least must-do spend is above the budget.

options.text: An error, since each start year of a must-do has to fit that year's budget
options.says: Only the least spend over the start years must fit; one start that fits is enough.

origin.section: Rules Across Projects Run Only on Clean Cells

questions.stem: Three exports of one portfolio: the second lists the assets in a different order and writes the discount rate as 0.07000000003; the third is like the first with one project's cost $10k higher. Which digests agree?

options.text: None of the three, since the files' bytes all differ from each other
options.says: The digest is of the canonical form, not the file: reordered rows and a float's last digits gave the same digest in the lesson.

options.text: The first and second agree, and the third has a digest of its own
options.says: Right: order and float noise vanish in the canonical form; P101's $10k change gave a new digest.

options.text: All three agree, since a $10k change is below the precision the digest keeps
options.says: Costs are whole $k and written exactly; only floats are cut to six decimals, and a $10k change gave 2d173fe29605.

options.text: The first and third agree, since record order is part of the content but costs are not
options.says: Records are sorted by id in the canonical form, so order is not content, and the cost change changed the digest.

origin.section: The Snapshot Is Named by the Hash of Its Canonical Content
